papers.title: Photon localization: Local measurements, localized states, and causality
papers.problem: What does it mean for a photon to be localized in quantum field theory, where there is no position operator, the vacuum is entangled across regions, and no-go theorems (Hegerfeldt, Malament, Reeh–Schlieder) seem to forbid localized particles altogether?
papers.result: The review argues that localization should be defined through local measurement: a state is strictly localized to a spacetime region \(\mathcal O\) if no observable outside \(\mathcal O\) can tell it from the vacuum. With this definition, single photons (and any state with a bounded photon number) cannot be strictly localized, while coherent states, squeezed states and states arbitrarily close to single photons can. On-demand sources must produce strictly localized states.
techniques: Prove non-localizability from a nonvanishing vacuum matrix element
Build localized states from the polar part of a smeared field

papers.title: Discrete Time Liquids
papers.authors: Zuo Wang; Paul M. Schindler; Marin Bukov; Marios H. Michael
papers.problem: Time crystals break the discrete time-translation symmetry of a perfectly periodic drive. Can temporal order also emerge from noise, when the only drive is the thermal fluctuation of a cavity mode with finite coherence time?
papers.result: Yes. A two-dimensional classical spin lattice coupled to a thermal cavity mode locks to half the cavity frequency within a window of bath temperatures. When the cavity coherence time is short, single trajectories switch stochastically between the two period-doubled configurations. These switches, called time-solitons, destroy long-range temporal coherence while preserving local period doubling: a discrete time liquid. A one-parameter toy model with independent sign flips reproduces the full distribution of single-trajectory correlation times.
techniques: Treat a narrow-band thermal mode as a random-amplitude, random-phase drive
Separate defects from decay with three nested correlation times

papers.title: Normal-Form Characterization of Adaptivity and Entanglement in Pauli-Based Computation
papers.authors: Filipa C. R. Peres; Selman Ipek; Daniel Lovsted; Joshua Nevin; Anne Broadbent
papers.problem: Pauli-based computation (PBC) runs a Clifford+\(T\) circuit as a sequence of commuting Pauli measurements on magic states, chosen adaptively from earlier outcomes. The adaptive tree of measurements is exponentially large. Is there a compact description of how branches differ, comparable to flow in one-way computing?
papers.result: Yes. Every branch of the PBC tree is obtained from the all-zero reference branch by conjugating each observable with phase gates \(S\) on the magic qubits whose earlier outcomes were 1. This normal form groups measurements into adaptive layers, gives a duality with a computation-specific one-way computation, detects unnecessary magic qubits in polynomial rather than exponential time, and allows ahead-of-time compilation. The resulting circuits use on average about 50% fewer CNOTs and 40% less quantum memory than state-of-the-art compilers on random circuits.
techniques: Move outcome-dependent corrections onto the input state
Detect removable resources by checking one branch against a symmetry

papers.title: Transversal syndrome extraction: A unifying construction for measuring the error syndromes of any stabilizer code
papers.problem: Fault-tolerant syndrome extraction for a general stabilizer code is either deep (Shor’s method measures one stabilizer at a time with cat states) or wide (Steane’s method measures everything at once with a \(2n\)-qubit encoded ancilla). Configurable middle grounds were known only for CSS codes. Is there one for every stabilizer code?
papers.result: Yes. Partitioning the stabilizer generators into sets measured together, and building a matching ancilla stabilizer state from the generalized Steane ancilla, gives a family of transversal gadgets for any stabilizer code. Shor and Steane extraction appear as the two limits, so depth can be traded for width. For example, the full syndrome of an \([[8,2,3]]\) code can be measured with four layers of data–ancilla gates using at most 12 ancilla qubits. Simulated logical error rates fall between those of Shor and Steane extraction.
techniques: Design ancillas so that propagated stabilizers carry the syndrome and nothing else
Interpolate between two known gadgets by deleting rows and qubits

papers.title: Pure states are optimal for total energy-constrained quantum channel discrimination
papers.problem: When discriminating two bosonic channels with a probe of fixed mean photon number and no ancilla, is a pure probe always optimal? Convexity suggests yes, but the pure components of a mixed probe generally have different photon numbers, so the best component may break the energy budget.
papers.result: Yes. Every state of mean photon number \(\bar n\) is a mixture of pure states each with mean photon number exactly \(\bar n\), including for infinite rank. Combined with Lieb concavity, this shows that for any two channels some equal-energy pure probe does at least as well as any mixed probe. This holds for the quantum Chernoff exponent, for every Chernoff quantity \(Q_s\), and for the single-shot error probability.
techniques: Equalize a constraint across a decomposition by pairwise rotations
From concavity at one \(s\) to optimality of the minimized exponent

papers.title: Distributed dual-comb spectroscopy
papers.authors: Haowei Shi; Kartikeya Arora; Zheshen Zhang; Quntao Zhuang
papers.problem: Quantum-enhanced dual-comb spectroscopy uses squeezed or entangled frequency combs to beat shot noise over a broad band, and distributed quantum sensing uses entanglement across sites to estimate global quantities. Can one combine both, estimating weighted averages of absorption across many samples and many frequencies, with a single quantum light source?
papers.result: Yes. Each sample sits in a Mach–Zehnder interferometer with a bright classical comb in one port and a share of a single two-mode-squeezed comb, split \(K\) ways by a passive beam splitter, in the dark port. With splitter weights matched to the target weights, the variance of every weighted-average estimator falls by the squeezing gain \(G\). Splitters that do not depend on frequency force a trade-off between gases with different targets: for orthogonal targets the guaranteed advantage is \(2G/(G+1)\), at most 3 dB.
techniques: Match the entanglement splitter to the estimated linear functional
Bound multi-target advantage by a shared-resource geometry

papers.title: What does quantum parameter estimation estimate? A no-go result for true quantity values
papers.authors: Jacques L. Pienaar; Eran Tal; Asya Ciftci
papers.problem: Quantum metrology speaks of estimating an unknown “true value”. Is that reading consistent when the estimated quantity is itself quantum and can become entangled with the probes?
papers.result: No, not without a cost. Embedding the parameter as an observable \(\hat\theta\) reproduces standard estimation whenever its state is diagonal. But five assumptions cannot all hold together: Uniqueness, Pre-existing Value and Independence (the realist reading of a true value), Entanglement between quantity and probes, and Completeness of the quantum state (no hidden variables). Dropping any one restores consistency.
techniques: Embed a classical parameter as a controlling quantum register
Locate a no-go theorem by listing jointly inconsistent assumptions

papers.title: Mixed State Deep Thermalization under Generic Quantum Errors
papers.problem: After chaotic dynamics, the states of a subsystem conditioned on measuring the rest follow a universal (Haar) distribution. What distribution emerges when local errors make those conditional states mixed?
papers.result: A universal one fixed by the error alone. The late-time ensemble of conditional states is the channel-induced ensemble, \(\tilde\rho=XMX^\dagger\) with \(X\) a complex Gaussian (Ginibre) matrix and Born weight \(\operatorname{Tr}XMX^\dagger\). Here \(M\) is the normalized Choi state of the error, and only its spectrum matters. This is derived for dual-unitary circuits, global Haar dynamics and local Haar circuits at large local dimension, and checked numerically in qubit circuits and kicked Ising dynamics.
techniques: A random-matrix reference ensemble built from the Choi state
Born-weighted moments of a projected ensemble

papers.title: The limits of magic-state distillation
papers.problem: How few noisy T states can any stabilizer protocol, however adaptive, postselected or multistage, consume to output a magic state with error \(O(p^d)\)?
papers.result: Exact minima for small factories. Fault tolerance of any protocol reduces to projection onto a single stabilizer code, and for rational targets a fault pattern is harmful exactly when its complement is. Exhaustive search then shows: quadratic distillation of one T state needs exactly 9 inputs (a new 9-input factory is found), controlled-S needs 8, and the 8-input CCZ factory is optimal. At every order \(d\), one T state needs at least \(2d\) inputs.
techniques: Reduce all protocols to one code projection
Galois conjugation pairs complementary faults

papers.title: Size-independent Logarithmic Sobolev Inequalities for Quantum Gibbs Samplers
papers.authors: Hongrui Chen; Zhiyan Ding; Jianfeng Lu
papers.problem: Does relative entropy decay at a rate independent of system size under quasi-local quantum Gibbs samplers for non-commuting Hamiltonians?
papers.result: Yes, in two regimes. For the Gaussian KMS Gibbs sampler, both the \(L^2\) logarithmic Sobolev inequality and the modified one (MLSI) hold with system-size-independent constants: in one dimension at every finite temperature, and in any fixed dimension at sufficiently high temperature. This gives \(O(\log n+\log(1/\epsilon))\) mixing time.
techniques: Transport a functional inequality along a unitary path
Upgrade Rényi-2 contraction to relative-entropy contraction with tensor powers

papers.title: One-shot entanglement generation and distillation via Petz recovery and binary hypothesis testing
papers.problem: How much entanglement can two laboratories obtain from one use of a noisy channel or one copy of a shared noisy state, and can the answer be expressed as a binary hypothesis-testing cost?
papers.result: An \((m,\varepsilon)\) entanglement generation or one-way distillation protocol exists whenever \(e_{d,m}(1-e_{d,m}/dm)\le\varepsilon\). Here \(e_{d,m}\) is the optimal error for testing \(\rho_{AB}\) against an explicit alternative \(B_{d,m}\propto dI_A\otimes\rho_B-\rho_{AB}\). Consequently \(\log_2m\le I_H^{\varepsilon-\nu}(A\rangle B)-\log_2(1/\nu)\) suffices, and repeated use gives \(nI_c+\sqrt{nV_c}\,\Phi^{-1}(\varepsilon)-\tfrac12\log_2n-c\) ebits.
techniques: Apply Cheng’s trace inequality before averaging over random codes
From a binary test to an integer code dimension

papers.title: A simple proof of unitary parallelization via port-based teleportation
papers.problem: Can port-based teleportation be implemented by an elementary low-depth circuit, and does that give a simple proof that every unitary can be parallelized?
papers.result: Yes. A single reflection on Alice’s registers implements port-based teleportation with \(N\) ports and dimension \(d\) to diamond error \(2(d^2-1)/N+\delta\), in depth \(\operatorname{polylog}(Nd/\delta)\). Feeding Choi states of \(U\) into the ports implements any \(n\)-qubit unitary in depth \(\operatorname{poly}(n,\log1/\varepsilon)\) and width \(2^{O(n)}\operatorname{poly}(1/\varepsilon)\).
techniques: Teleport with a single reflection
Read out sums of swaps with parallel random SWAP tests

papers.title: Conservation in Every Quantum Measurement Outcome?
papers.authors: E. Okon; D. Sudarsky; M. Wiedemann
papers.problem: Does including the system that prepared a superposition restore a conservation law in every individual measurement outcome, as Collins and Popescu have proposed?
papers.result: The authors argue that it does not, in the sense claimed. The need for a physical preparer is postulated rather than derived from the relativity of angle. The preparer never holds a definite value, so what the mechanism restores is a shifted probability distribution. A preparation that conserves one observable can disturb a noncommuting one. For energy, the preparation interaction breaks the additivity the bookkeeping relies on.
techniques: Test a conservation mechanism against the whole symmetry group
Overlap factors set how broad a hidden partner must be

papers.title: An entanglement band structure for general multiqubit states
papers.problem: Majorana pictured a symmetric multiqubit state as points on the sphere. Can a comparable geometric picture be given for general states, whose entanglement classes form continuous families?
papers.result: Projecting one qubit onto a direction \(\mathbf n\) leaves a conditional state of the others. Its entanglement invariants are the eigenvalues, called bands, of a non-Hermitian matrix \(L(u)\). For five qubits there are four bands, which meet at 24 exceptional points where the conditional state changes entanglement family. Together they form one Riemann surface of genus nine, which fixes the five-qubit entanglement class up to finitely many choices.
techniques: Read SLOCC invariants from a holomorphic matrix pencil
Count exceptional points and the genus from the discriminant

papers.title: Injection is all you need: parallel universal logic in high-rate concatenated self-dual codes
papers.authors: Joseph Sullivan; David Amaro; Michael A. Perlin
papers.problem: High-rate codes store many logical qubits per block but make it hard to act on a chosen subset. How can they run parallel, addressable, universal logic?
papers.result: In concatenated self-dual codes with transversal global \(H\) and \(S\), any logical Clifford is injected by consuming at most 9 CSS resource states. \(T\) gates on any subset need one \(\ket H^{\otimes K}\) magic state and one CSS state, so a circuit of \(T\)-depth \(D_T\) needs at most \(12D_T\) resource states. A Hadamard parity check repeated at each concatenation level gives magic states whose undetected error is \(O(p^{2^L})\). In simulations at \(p=5\times10^{-4}\), this concatenated cultivation needed about ten times less spacetime than surface-code cultivation for the two distance-4 codes.
techniques: Reduce every Clifford layer to CSS resource states
Hadamard-parity flags, and why one parity stalls at second order

papers.title: Finite Classification of Transversal Diagonal Gates Beyond Stabilizer Codes
papers.authors: Xi He; Chao Zhang; Shilin Huang; Bei Zeng
papers.problem: Code-preserving diagonal phases of general (nonadditive) qubit codes can vary continuously. Can the transversal diagonal gates of such codes still be classified exhaustively?
papers.result: Yes, at fixed code parameters. For a code of distance at least two, every projective logical action of a transversal diagonal gate has a physical representative of finite order \(q\), with \(m\mid q\) and \(q\) bounded in terms of \(n\) and \(K\) alone; \(q\le9\) for six qubits at distance three. For exact ((6,2,3)) codes, 66 candidate symmetry classes reduce to 15 realizable ones, with diagonal logical groups \(C_2\), \(C_3\) or \(C_5\). The order-five code is unique up to local unitaries and qubit permutations. It is also the shortest distance-3 qubit code whose transversal logical group cannot be conjugated into the Clifford group.
techniques: Strip continuous phases that act only as logical scalars
Subset-sum sectors and moment matching as a staged filter

papers.title: Tight Bounds on the Randomized Communication Complexity of Vector-in-Subspace
papers.problem: One quantum message of \(\lceil\log_2n\rceil\) qubits solves Vector-in-Subspace exactly. How many bits does an interactive classical protocol need?
papers.result: \(\Theta(\sqrt n)\) bits. A lower bound of \(\Omega(\sqrt n)\) holds for bounded-error randomized protocols with any number of rounds, matching Raz’s \(O(\sqrt n)\) protocol. It improves the \(\Omega(n^{1/3})\) bound of Klartag and Regev and removes the total-rank restriction in Grupel’s \(\Omega(\sqrt n)\) result.
techniques: Complex Gaussian lifts perform the Wick corrections
A vanishing even moment bounds a real center

papers.title: Quantum f-divergences from retrodiction: a unifying classical variational principle
papers.problem: A classical \(f\)-divergence has several inequivalent quantum extensions. Can they all be obtained from one operational optimization?
papers.result: Yes. Compare a forward prepare-and-measure process with its reverse, obtained by Petz retrodiction relative to a reference prior \(\gamma\), subject to prescribed averages \(\rho\) and \(\sigma\). The minimum classical \(f\)-divergence between their complete records is attained by one spectral implementation, simultaneously for every operator-convex \(f\). A flat prior gives the standard (Petz) divergence, Umegaki for relative entropy. A prior equal to \(\rho\) or \(\sigma\) gives the maximal divergence, Belavkin–Staszewski for relative entropy, and power priors \(\gamma\propto\sigma^t\) give the geodesic family between them.
techniques: Two operator-Jensen steps remove the implementation freedom
The retrodiction prior selects the quantum divergence

papers.title: Dimension-free marginal inequalities for pure three-party states
papers.problem: Which spectra can the three one-party marginals of a pure three-party state have, with inequalities that hold in every local dimension?
papers.result: A lifting theorem produces new valid inequalities from old ones by peeling off one party’s largest Schmidt component and applying Horn’s inequalities to the other two. Starting from Klyachko’s first-row bound, at most two lifting steps reproduce every facet of the marginal polytope for local dimension up to 4, and 455 of the 466 facet classes for dimension 5.
techniques: Peel off the largest Schmidt component
Combine Horn triples with Abel summation

papers.title: Trapped-ion-based quantum repeater node across a 17 km metropolitan fiber
papers.authors: K. Fabitha; T. Runggaldier; A. Winkler; F. Bernecker; J. Bate; M. Canteri; J. Helgert; T. E. Northup; V. Krutyanskiy; B. P. Lanyon
papers.problem: Can a trapped-ion repeater node distribute entanglement over deployed city fiber rather than a laboratory spool?
papers.result: A two-ion node in Innsbruck entangled a photon sent through 17 km of rented municipal fiber with a photon detected locally. The Bell-state fidelity was \(81.6^{+1.9}_{-1.4}\%\) (with feed-forward simulated), at 0.69 successes per second. Storing the first ion qubit raised the success probability 13.6-fold over sending both photons without memory.
techniques: Store the qubit for the fast link, not the slow one
Correct a drifting fiber by tomography and inversion

papers.title: The Four-Qubit Hyperbolic Quadric Has Contextuality Degree 315
papers.authors: Zhengyu Li; Amandeep Gupta; Vijay Ganesh
papers.problem: How many of the 1575 three-observable constraints on a four-qubit hyperbolic quadric must every noncontextual value assignment break?
papers.result: Exactly 315, proving a conjecture based on heuristic searches. In every optimal assignment each of the 40,320 doilies has exactly three violated lines, and the 240 possible violated sets are all copies of the dual polar space DW(5,2).
techniques: Read a lower bound from parity alone
Average over a symmetric cover, rounding locally

papers.title: Polynomial-Time Classical Simulation of BosonSampling under Any Constant-Fraction Photon Loss
papers.problem: Does lossy BosonSampling remain hard to simulate classically when a fixed fraction of the photons survives?
papers.result: Not under the conditions studied. For every fixed survival fraction \(n/N\in(0,1)\), Haar-random interferometers and \(M=\Omega(n^2N)\) modes, a classical algorithm samples within total variation distance \(\varepsilon\) of the collision-collapsed output distribution, for a \(1-\delta\) fraction of interferometers, in time \(\mathrm{poly}(M,N,\varepsilon^{-1},\delta^{-1})\). The same holds for every fixed transmission probability \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
techniques: Decompose an average over random survivors
Sum over subsets with color coding

papers.title: Correlated decoding loses the surface code’s effective distance below threshold
papers.authors: César Hernando de la Fuente; Joonas Majaniemi; Evert van Nieuwenburg; Felix Frohnert
papers.problem: Does two-pass correlated decoding of the surface code keep its advantage far below threshold?
papers.result: Not with the standard reweighting rule. Under circuit-level noise some size-\((d-1)/2\) fault configurations cause logical failures, so the logical error rate scales like \(p^{(d-1)/2}\) instead of \(p^{(d+1)/2}\). At \(d=3\) and \(p=10^{-5}\), correlated matching fails about 4.4 times as often as plain matching. Scaling the conditional edge probabilities by an error-rate-dependent factor \(\alpha^*(p)\) restores the distance scaling and a steady advantage.
techniques: Count the independent faults behind a correction
Regularize the update with one error-rate-dependent parameter

papers.title: Randomness Certification from Statistically Hiding Commitments
papers.problem: What cryptographic assumption lets a classical verifier certify randomness from a single untrusted quantum device, secure against quantum side information?
papers.result: A statistically hiding bit commitment that is computationally binding against quantum senders suffices; stronger notions such as collapse-binding are not needed. Consequently, post-quantum one-way permutations suffice. Trapdoor claw-free functions give an efficient verifier, and the quantum random-oracle model gives certification with no further assumption but an inefficient verifier.
techniques: Hide a BB84 basis inside two commitment openings
Turn a predictor into two openings

papers.title: Pump-Free Microwave-Optical Bell Pair Generation for Teleportation-Based Quantum Transduction
papers.problem: How can superconducting processors connect to optical networks while avoiding complications from optical pumping?
papers.result: Spin-mediated sources are predicted to herald microwave–optical Bell pairs at roughly 1–28 kHz, with fidelities of 0.86–0.99 depending on the platform. The pairs are intended for teleportation-based transduction.
techniques: Separate resource generation from state transfer
Use an intermediate spin as an interface

papers.title: Information Causality Characterizes the Set of Quantum Correlations in the Simplest Bell Scenario
papers.problem: Can an information principle recover the quantum boundary in the simplest Bell experiment?
papers.result: Generalized information causality implies the Tsirelson–Landau–Masanes criterion on the four renormalized correlators, so it recovers the quantum boundary of that correlator projection. A separate example shows that it also excludes some correlations that macroscopic locality allows.
techniques: Keep the full measurement record
Expand around zero capacity

papers.title: Spurious quantum correlations
papers.authors: Shashaank Khanna; Matthew F. Pusey; Roger Colbeck
papers.problem: Can correlations that appear nonclassical acquire a classical explanation when the assumed causal structure changes?
papers.result: The authors identify correlations with classical explanations in alternative causal structures without fine tuning, and other correlations that resist such explanations.
techniques: Search over causal explanations
Separate statistical fit from physical admissibility

papers.title: Quantum error correction at ultra-low overhead
papers.authors: Zhide Lu; Weikang Li; Dong-Ling Deng
papers.problem: Can quantum error-correcting codes combine high encoding rates, tolerable noise, and feasible neutral-atom operations?
papers.result: Cornucopia codes reach encoding rates just above 1/2 at distances 6 to 18 and pseudo-thresholds above 0.4% under circuit-level noise. Their 12-layer syndrome cycle is carried out by rigid moves of whole atom blocks.
techniques: Design the code and its circuit together
Certify distance and count resources consistently

papers.title: A solution to 2-copy distillability of Werner states
papers.authors: Jinshi Fu; Li Gao; Sang-Jun Park
papers.problem: Can two copies of a Werner state yield distillable entanglement when one copy cannot?
papers.result: For every local dimension \(d\), a Werner state \(\rho_\alpha\) is two-copy distillable exactly when it is one-copy distillable (\(\alpha<-\tfrac12\)). States with \(-\tfrac12\le\alpha<-\tfrac1d\) are therefore NPT but not two-copy distillable.
techniques: Turn distillation into an operator test
Use symmetry to isolate a boundary case

papers.title: Quantum error correction with the toric code
papers.problem: Can neutral-atom logical memories sustain repeated error correction while replacing lost atoms?
papers.result: Twisted toric-code memories on 32 and 64 atoms (\([[16,1,(4,3)]]\) and \([[32,1,(6,4)]]\)) run for up to 90 and 70 syndrome cycles with atom reloading. Over four to eight cycles, the larger code has the lower logical error.
techniques: Rotate data and ancilla roles
Make replenishment part of the computation
